dedupe_keys.name: anuar caracteristica hidrologica annual hydrological yearbook of moldova state hydrometeorological service 2022 edition

description: The hydrological yearbook of Moldova's State Hydrometeorological Service summarises each year the state of the country's rivers and reservoirs. The 2022 edition read on 2026-09-28, a 92-page PDF published in 2023 by the service's Hydrological Centre, describes month by month the flow of the Dniester, the Prut and small rivers such as the Răut, Ichel and Botna at gauging posts of the national hydrological monitoring network, comparing monthly discharges with long-term norms and absolute maxima and minima reaching back to the 1940s and 1950s, and covers spring high waters, ice phenomena and dangerous hydrological events, with notes on the Dnestrovsk and Costești-Stânca reservoirs that regulate the two main rivers. Coverage is the surface waters of the Republic of Moldova. The yearbook is free to download and no licence is stated. Caveats: the data are in narrative text and tables of a PDF in Romanian, not a machine-readable series, and only one edition was read, so the span of earlier editions is unconfirmed. It supports flood and drought studies, such as calibrating river flow extremes for bridge, water intake or levee design on the Dniester and Prut. No related Moldovan hydrological record is catalogued.

sources.note: read pages 1-8 (the yearbook page redirects to this PDF): Caracteristica hidrologica, Anuar 2022, Serviciul Hidrometeorologic de Stat, Chisinau 2023; 92 pages; monthly hydrological characteristics January-December and the surface water regime of 2022; annual publication with analysed information on the quantitative state and evolution of surface waters for each basin and sub-basin; spring high waters and ice phenomena; national hydrological monitoring network (RNMH); monthly flows with long-term norms and absolute maxima and minima, e.g. Nistru at Hrusca (January mean 232 m3/s, maximum 1190 m3/s on 06.01.1982), Prut at Siruati, small rivers such as Raut, Ichel, Botna; Dnestrovsk reservoir in operation since 1982 and Costesti-Stanca since 1978
